questions.stem: Which is a benefit of starting a business for the owner?
options: protection from losing any of the money invested
fewer working hours than most employees work
independence to make decisions and keep the profits
a guaranteed income from the first month of trading
questions.explanation: Owners gain independence, the chance to keep the profits and the satisfaction of building something of their own. Income is not guaranteed, and many new owners work longer hours than employees.

questions.stem: Opportunity cost is best defined as:
options: the value of the next best alternative given up
the total amount spent to start a new business
the profit earned in the first year of trading
the interest paid on money borrowed for a business
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is what is sacrificed when a choice is made: the benefit of the best option not taken. Start-up spending is a financial cost, not the opportunity cost itself.

questions.stem: Mia leaves a job paying $78,000 a year to open a cafe in Newtown. In its first year the cafe makes a profit of $45,000. What is the opportunity cost of Mia's time for that year?
options: $45,000, the profit the cafe made
$33,000, the gap between the two
$123,000, the salary plus profit
$78,000, the salary she gave up
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of her time is the next best alternative forgone, the $78,000 salary. The $33,000 gap is how much worse off she is in money terms, not the opportunity cost.

questions.stem: A sole trader borrows $60,000 against her home to start a business in Orange. The business fails and cannot repay the loan. What is the main financial risk she faces?
options: the bank must write off the whole loan because the business has now closed
she loses only the money she had put into the business so far
the government repays the loans of businesses that fail early
her personal assets, including her home, may be used to repay the debt
questions.explanation: A sole trader has unlimited liability, and the loan is secured against her home, so she can lose personal assets as well as her savings. Lenders do not write off loans simply because a business closes.

questions.stem: Josh uses $40,000 of savings that earned 4% interest a year to start a business, and gives up a job paying $70,000. His business makes a profit of $30,000 in its first year. Compared with staying in his job and keeping his savings, Josh is:
options: $41,600 worse off for the year
$30,000 better off for the year
$40,000 worse off for the year
$1,600 worse off for the year
questions.explanation: Forgone income is $70,000 salary plus $1,600 interest (4% of $40,000) = $71,600, and $30,000 - $71,600 = -$41,600. Counting the profit alone ignores the opportunity cost of his job and savings.

questions.stem: Struggling to find a dog walker who suits her shift work, a Parramatta nurse starts an app that matches dog owners with local walkers. The source of her idea is best described as:
options: a copy of a successful overseas business
a new technology she invented herself
a problem she experienced personally
a hobby that she turned into a business
questions.explanation: Many ideas come from a frustration the founder has experienced, which suggests others share the problem. The app uses existing technology rather than a new invention.

questions.stem: A keen home baker in Albury begins selling her sourdough at weekend markets. The source of this business idea is best described as:
options: a gap found by surveying rivals
a change in government policy
a trend in overseas markets
a hobby or personal skill
questions.explanation: Turning a hobby or skill into a business is a common source of ideas, because the founder already has knowledge and enthusiasm. Nothing in the scenario points to research on rivals, policy or overseas trends.

questions.stem: Seeing the number of electric vehicles on the road grow, a Penrith mechanic retrains and opens a workshop that services them. The source of this idea is:
options: a personal hobby of the mechanic
a franchise bought from a large chain
a complaint from a single customer
a technological and social trend
questions.explanation: Spotting a trend, such as the shift to electric vehicles, lets a business meet new demand early. The idea comes from a change in the market, not a hobby or a franchise offer.

questions.stem: A subscription business model earns revenue by:
options: taking a commission on each sale made between other parties
selling advertising space to other businesses
charging customers a regular fee for ongoing access
selling each item once at a single fixed price
questions.explanation: Subscriptions charge a recurring weekly, monthly or yearly fee, as with streaming services or meal kits. Taking a commission on others' sales describes a marketplace model.

questions.stem: A study app is free to download, but users can pay a monthly fee to unlock extra features. This business model is best described as:
options: freemium
franchising
marketplace
wholesaling
questions.explanation: A freemium model gives a basic version away to attract many users and earns revenue from those who pay for premium features. A marketplace earns commission by connecting buyers and sellers.

questions.stem: An online platform connects Sydney homeowners with local tradespeople and charges the tradespeople a fee on each job booked. This is:
options: a freemium model with paid upgrades
a marketplace model earning a commission
a subscription model charging monthly fees
a manufacturing model making its goods
questions.explanation: A marketplace or platform model brings buyers and sellers together and earns a fee or commission on each transaction. The platform does not provide the trade services itself.

questions.stem: Which is the main advantage of a subscription model over one-off sales for a new business?
options: customers cannot cancel once they have subscribed
customers need not be kept happy after signing up
a higher price can be charged for each single item
more predictable, recurring revenue to plan cash flow
questions.explanation: Regular payments from subscribers make revenue easier to forecast and support cash flow planning. Subscribers can usually cancel, so keeping them satisfied remains essential.

questions.stem: A new online marketplace for second-hand school uniforms has few buyers because it has few sellers, and few sellers because it has few buyers. This shows that a marketplace model:
options: must hold large stocks of every product listed by its sellers
cannot earn revenue from either the buyers or the sellers
must manufacture the products that its sellers offer for sale
must attract enough buyers and sellers for either to find value
questions.explanation: A platform is only useful when both sides are active, so new marketplaces often subsidise one side to build the other. Marketplaces usually hold no stock and earn commissions or listing fees.

questions.stem: Entrepreneurial innovation is best described as:
options: registering a business name and an ABN with government
raising prices to increase the business's profit margin
turning a new idea into a product or process that creates value
copying a rival's product exactly and selling it for less
questions.explanation: Innovation means putting new or improved ideas into practice so that they create value for customers and the business. Copying a rival's product is imitation, not innovation.

questions.stem: A Newcastle surf shop adds a click-and-collect option to its existing website. Compared with inventing a new type of surfboard, this is best described as:
options: market research, gathering primary data from customers
competitor analysis, finding a gap left by rival stores
incremental innovation, a small improvement to what exists
radical innovation, creating an entirely new type of product
questions.explanation: Incremental innovation improves an existing product, service or process step by step. A completely new surfboard design would be closer to radical innovation.

questions.stem: A student proposes a reusable lunchbox subscription for schools. Which evidence would best justify the idea to an investor?
options: the founder's strong personal belief that the idea will succeed
a list of extra features the founder plans to add in future
the total number of schools in NSW, taken from a website
paid pre-orders from 120 families after a trial at two schools
questions.explanation: Justifying a new idea needs evidence that customers will pay, and paid pre-orders after a trial are strong evidence of demand. The number of schools shows the market's size, not whether anyone will buy.

questions.stem: The main purpose of defining a target market is to:
options: make sure the product appeals equally to everyone
meet the legal requirements for registering a business
work out the rate of company tax the business pays
focus marketing on the customers most likely to buy
questions.explanation: A clear target market lets a business tailor its product, price, promotion and location to the customers it can serve best. Trying to appeal to everyone usually means appealing strongly to no one.

questions.stem: A Coffs Harbour start-up defines its target market as retirees who travel in caravans. Which decision follows most directly from this?
options: opening a large shopfront in the centre of the Sydney CBD
matching its prices to those of luxury car manufacturers
advertising in caravan club magazines and at caravan parks
advertising on the music apps that are most popular with teenagers
questions.explanation: Knowing the target market tells the business where and how to reach its customers, here through caravan clubs and parks. The other choices do not match the needs or habits of travelling retirees.

questions.stem: The main role of market research for a new business is to:
options: guarantee that the new product will sell well once it is launched
replace the need for a business plan when seeking finance
register the business with the Australian Business Register
reduce risk by providing evidence about customers and the market
questions.explanation: Market research gives the owner evidence on demand, customers and competitors so that decisions are less of a guess. It reduces risk but cannot guarantee success.

questions.stem: Primary data is information that:
options: is found only in government reports and statistics
comes from a rival's annual report or its website
a business collects first-hand for its own purpose
has already been published by others, such as the ABS
questions.explanation: Primary data is new information collected by the business itself, for example through surveys, interviews, focus groups or observation. Data already published by others is secondary data.

questions.stem: Which is secondary data for the owners of a planned gym in Wagga Wagga?
options: a survey of 150 local residents run by the owners
a focus group of possible members held at the site
a count of people entering a rival gym over one week
an industry report on gym membership trends in Australia
questions.explanation: An industry report was collected by someone else for another purpose, so it is secondary data. Surveys, focus groups and observation counts run by the owners are all primary data.

questions.stem: Why does a larger sample size usually give more reliable market research results?
options: a larger sample turns the information into secondary data instead
a larger sample means the questions no longer need careful wording
random variation has less effect, so results better reflect the market
a larger sample always removes bias from the way people were chosen
questions.explanation: With more responses, chance differences between individuals average out, so the results are closer to the whole market. A large sample chosen in a biased way is still biased.

questions.stem: A Dubbo start-up plans a product for local families and surveys only its own Instagram followers. What is the main problem with this sample?
options: online surveys cannot be used to collect any data
it may not be representative of all local families
it produces secondary data rather than primary data
it is too large a sample to analyse with accuracy
questions.explanation: Followers already like the business and may differ from typical local families, so the sample is not representative. A representative sample reflects the make-up of the whole target market.

questions.stem: A start-up surveys 400 randomly chosen households in its area: 140 say they would 'definitely' buy its meal kits. Which interpretation is most valid?
options: exactly 35% of all households in the area will become customers
about 14% may buy, so the business should not go ahead at all
the result is useless, because a sample of 400 is far too small
about 35% may buy, but stated intentions often overstate real sales
questions.explanation: 140 / 400 = 35%. What people say in a survey is often higher than what they later spend, so the figure is an upper estimate rather than a forecast. A random sample of 400 is a reasonable size.

questions.stem: A start-up wants to test interest in a premium dog food among NSW dog owners. Which sample would give the most reliable results?
options: 300 dog owners chosen at random from across NSW
1,000 visitors to a large dog show held in Sydney
50 dog owners chosen at random from across NSW
300 friends and relatives of the two founders
questions.explanation: A random sample from the whole target market that is reasonably large is both representative and reliable. Dog show visitors and friends are biased groups, and 50 people is a small sample.

questions.stem: Competitor analysis helps a new business mainly by:
options: identifying gaps in the market that rivals are not meeting
making sure its prices are exactly the same as its rivals'
removing any need for it to research its own customers
stopping competitors from entering the same market
questions.explanation: Studying rivals' products, prices, locations and weaknesses reveals unmet needs the new business can target. It complements, rather than replaces, research on customers.

questions.stem: A competitor analysis of cafes near Macquarie University shows that all of them close at 4 pm and none offers vegan meals. Which market gap does this suggest?
options: standard menus served between 7 am and 4 pm
a wider range of breakfasts that are not vegan
a cafe located further from the university
vegan meals and evening opening for students
questions.explanation: A gap is a need that existing businesses are not meeting, here evening trade and vegan food. Copying what every rival already offers does not fill a gap.

questions.stem: A map of Penrith restaurants by price and healthiness shows rivals clustered as 'low price, less healthy' or 'high price, healthy'. Before targeting 'low price, healthy', the owner should most importantly:
options: copy the menu and prices of the most successful rival
register a trade mark for the restaurant's name first
check through research that customers want that combination
open at once, since any gap in the market guarantees profit
questions.explanation: A gap is only an opportunity if enough customers want it and the business can serve it profitably. Some gaps exist because demand is too small or costs are too high.

questions.stem: A minimum viable product (MVP) is:
options: the number of sales a business needs to make to break even
a basic version with just enough features to test on real customers
the final product with every feature, sold at the lowest price
the smallest order quantity that a supplier is willing to accept
questions.explanation: An MVP lets a business learn from real customers quickly and cheaply before investing in a full product. Break-even sales and minimum orders are unrelated ideas.

questions.stem: The purpose of market validation is to:
options: confirm that customers will pay for an idea before investing heavily
obtain government approval for a product before it can be sold
show investors the founder has registered the business name
make sure that no competitor can copy the product once launched
questions.explanation: Validation tests the idea against real demand, for example through pre-orders or a trial, to cut the risk of building something nobody buys. It is not a legal approval or a form of protection from copying.

questions.stem: A Sydney founder tests a meal-prep idea with a simple web page. Of 2,000 visitors, 60 pay for a pre-order. Which conclusion is most valid?
options: 60% paid in advance, well above most start-ups
3% paid in advance, early evidence of real demand
30% paid in advance, so demand is already proven
0.3% paid in advance, so the idea should be dropped
questions.explanation: 60 / 2,000 = 3%. Paying in advance is stronger evidence than saying 'yes' in a survey, and the founder can now test and refine the offer. One small test does not prove demand.

questions.stem: Feedback on an MVP fitness app shows users ignore its main feature but use a secondary feature every day. The founders should most likely:
options: refocus the product on the feature that customers value
add more functions to the main feature before relaunching
ignore the feedback because early users are not typical
launch the full product unchanged to recover their costs
questions.explanation: The point of an MVP is to learn what customers value and adjust, sometimes called a pivot. Ignoring the evidence defeats the purpose of testing.

questions.stem: Brand development for a new business includes creating its:
options: ABN, GST registration and first BAS
legal structure and its owners
insurance policies and premiums
business name, logo and packaging
questions.explanation: A brand is built through the name, logo, packaging and the image these create in customers' minds. Registrations and insurance are legal and financial matters.

questions.stem: A new Mudgee winery names itself 'Red Gum Ridge' and uses hand-drawn gum leaves on its labels. The main purpose of these choices is to:
options: protect the name from copying in the same way as a patent
create an identity that customers recognise and remember
meet a legal requirement for the design of wine labels
lower the production cost of each bottle of wine
questions.explanation: A distinctive name and design help the product stand out and build recognition and loyalty. Names and logos are protected by trade marks, not patents.

questions.stem: Which is the main role of packaging as part of branding?
options: it allows the business to avoid displaying any of its product prices
it replaces the need for the business to have a logo
it ensures the product will meet the consumer guarantees
it protects the product and communicates the brand when buying
questions.explanation: Packaging protects the product and is often the first thing a shopper sees, so its design signals quality and brand identity at the point of sale. It works alongside, not instead of, the logo.

questions.stem: Referral marketing involves:
options: selling its products through wholesalers and retailers
cutting prices to win customers away from rivals
encouraging existing customers to recommend the business
paying for advertisements on television and radio
questions.explanation: Referral marketing turns satisfied customers into promoters, often with a reward for each new customer they bring. Paid mass advertising is a different form of promotion.

questions.stem: A new Wollongong physiotherapy clinic gives existing clients a free session for each friend who books. Why does this suit a small business?
options: it guarantees that every referred friend becomes a regular client
it removes the need for the clinic to provide good service
people trust friends' recommendations, and each one costs little
it reaches a national audience at the same time as a TV advertisement
questions.explanation: Recommendations from people we know are highly trusted, and a referral reward costs less than most advertising. Referrals only work if existing clients are happy with the service.

questions.stem: Why should a new plumber in Gosford set up a website and an online business listing with reviews?
options: having a website means the business no longer needs any insurance
online reviews can be removed by the business whenever it likes
local customers searching online can find, contact and assess the business
an online listing removes the need to register a business name with ASIC
questions.explanation: Many customers search online for local services, so an online presence with reviews helps them find and trust a new business. It does not replace legal registrations.

questions.stem: A new candle maker's costs are $12 a candle. Similar handmade candles sell for $25 to $30, and its target market is gift shoppers who value handmade products. Which price is most sensible?
options: about $28, covering costs and matching rivals and buyers
$10, so that it undercuts every competitor in the market
$60, because gift shoppers never take any notice of price
$12, so that each sale exactly covers the cost of a candle
questions.explanation: Price should cover costs, be competitive with similar products and suit what the target market will pay. Pricing below cost makes a loss on every sale, and pricing at cost leaves no profit.

questions.stem: A new skincare brand aimed at high-income customers sets its price below supermarket brands to win sales quickly. What is the main risk?
options: the low price means the brand cannot register a trade mark for its name
the low price will raise the cost of making each unit of the product
the low price may weaken its premium image with its target market
the low price will make it illegal to sell through department stores
questions.explanation: Price signals quality, so a price well below expectations can make premium buyers doubt the product, and margins may not cover costs. Price does not affect trade mark rights or unit costs.
